subject: Stratus Labs renewal — competitive replacement risk & capacity assurance
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@stratuslabs.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Nicole Tran <nicole.tran@stratuslabs.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Stratus Labs renewal: throughput concerns and vendor bake-off

Jordan,

Quick note — our procurement team flagged an inbound push from one of the other inference vendors. They've offered a month-long bake-off and are promising a 30% price reduction on equivalent throughput. We like Redwood's reliability, but two things are putting us on edge: 1) the recent tail-latency spikes in late May during our marketing peak, and 2) overall unit cost when scaled to our projected Q4 traffic.

We have a renewal coming up August 15 and the execs want a concrete plan by next week that addresses: capacity guarantees for seasonal spikes, objective bake-off rules (what you will demonstrate), and any commercial adjustments you can make to keep us from running the vendor PoC.

Can you outline a containment/save plan (technical + commercial) and confirm availability for a quick sync on Monday? Nicole and legal are on copy — they'll need the SLA language and any sample terms.

Thanks,
Samir
Director of AI Platform
Stratus Labs

[Attachment: stratus_capacity_report_May2027.pdf]

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@stratuslabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Stratus Labs renewal: throughput concerns and vendor bake-off

Samir — appreciate the heads up. Short answer: we do not want to lose Stratus. I can put a targeted containment plan together today and propose an accelerated technical bakeoff/happy path for next week. High-level items we'll commit to now: 1) a short-term dedicated pool for your peak campaigns (guaranteed burst headroom), 2) a focused bench test plan that targets your top-10 endpoints and worst-case sequence lengths, and 3) a commercial bridge: a limited renewal amendment that adds reserved capacity credits if latency targets are missed during the bakeoff.

Marissa — I need a concise capacity/ops summary and the latest telemetry Samir sent (I see the May report). Ben/Laura — I may ask you to weigh in on discount structure and term language.

Samir — can you do 30 minutes Monday 2027-06-21 at 10:00 PT? If that doesn't work, propose two slots. We'll circulate an agenda and a proposed measurement plan ahead of time.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | (415) 555-0193

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@stratuslabs.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 19 Jun 2027 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Stratus Labs renewal: throughput concerns and vendor bake-off

Jordan / Samir — attaching our quick rollup from the infra team. Summary: Stratus traffic patterns show two notable weekly peaks (marketing blasts and end-of-month report generation). Peak QPS 4.2x baseline, median P95 latency at baseline load is 110ms, but during the May surge we observed P99s climb to ~780ms on a small subset of requests. We have already isolated a few misrouted long-sequence calls and transient autoscaler lag as contributing factors.

Immediate ops steps we recommend for the bakeoff window:
- Provision a temporary dedicated GPU pool equivalent to 1.5x your current committed GPUs for a 4-week window
- Prewarm KV cache and pin the top-20 prompt prefixes
- Lock the DLLs / runtime kernel selection for repeatability during benchmarking

Attachments: stratus_capacity_report_May2027.pdf (original), bakeoff-instructions.md (test harness + metrics), quick-ops-rollup.txt

I'll highlight the P99 regression triggers in the meeting and walk through mitigations.

— Marissa
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: bakeoff-instructions.md]

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@stratuslabs.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Nicole Tran <nicole.tran@stratuslabs.com>, Stratus Labs Legal <legal@stratuslabs.com>
Date: Sat, 19 Jun 2027 13:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Stratus Labs renewal: throughput concerns and vendor bake-off

Thanks, Marissa / Jordan. Monday at 10:00 PT works. For the bakeoff we need a reproducible harness (scorecard we can share with procurement) and a hard go/no-go checklist. Procurement has asked that the bakeoff cover:
- Throughput at 1x, 2x, and 4x baseline for sustained 30-minute windows
- P95 and P99 on our longest prompt distributions and on edge-case sessions that use long context
- Cold-start and steady-state throughput for RAG-style requests with external vector stores
- Disk/network I/O stress paths (our infra team is particularly sensitive)

Legal would also like sample SLA language and a proposed 60-day interim credit if the bakeoff shows regressions beyond agreed thresholds. I'm copying Nicole + legal so they see the agenda.

Also: we intend to run the vendor PoC simultaneously next week; your three-hour test run needs to be deterministic and defensible to procurement.

Samir

On a separate note, is there a pragmatic commercial anchor you can offer now (not the final term) to signal commitment? Even a one-time renewal credit tied to a committed reserved capacity would help the internal talk track.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@stratuslabs.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Stratus Labs renewal: throughput concerns and vendor bake-off

Samir / Jordan — placing the technical plan here so procurement has a clear sense of test reproducibility. Key points:
1) Harness: our bakeoff-instructions.md contains the exact client call sequences, seed data, and traffic driver configs. We'll run three deterministic passes (1x / 2x / 4x) using the same seed set. Results exported as CSV + Grafana dashboards.
2) Environment: dedicated pool with pinned quantization profile (int8-optimized), fixed kernel selection, and KV cache prewarm. We will snapshot the runtime so hot-paths are identical across passes.
3) Measurements: P50/P95/P99, tail latency distribution, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, cache hit rate, and end-to-end RAG latency with vector store calls (we will run your vector store emulator to keep tests self-contained).
4) Runbook: automated canary rollback if P99 > 500ms for 3 consecutive minutes during a sustained 30-minute window.

I'll also include a small stress harness for disk/IO (fio-based) and a network emulation step. If procurement wants us to share the harness code, we can provide a read-only link to a test bucket.

Attaching: bakeoff-instructions.md

- Karthik
Principal Systems Engineer — Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@stratuslabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Stratus Labs Legal <legal@stratuslabs.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 17:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Stratus Labs renewal: throughput concerns and vendor bake-off

Samir — thanks for the clear asks and for confirming Monday. After syncing with the team, here's a pragmatic save package we can present in Monday's meeting (this is an interim commercial anchor, not the full amendment):

1) Temporary Dedicated Pool: Redwood will provision a dedicated GPU pool sized to 1.5x current committed capacity for a 30-day bakeoff window at no additional cost.
2) Performance Guarantee: If during the benchmark runs (per the agreed harness) P99 exceeds 500ms on the target endpoints for the sustained 30-minute windows, Redwood will provide a one-time credit equal to 20% of the monthly committed capacity fee for the following billing cycle.
3) Reserved Capacity Pilot Discount: If Stratus signs a 12-month reserved capacity addendum within 30 days of renewal, we will apply a one-time upfront credit equal to two weeks of reserved capacity usage (applied to the first invoice).
4) Deterministic Bakeoff: Karthik will execute the harness and share the raw CSVs and Grafana dashboard links; we will synchronize runs with your procurement schedule so both PoCs run concurrently.
5) Legal / SLA: Laura, can you please prepare a redlineable sample SLA that includes the interim credit language above and an audit clause for the bakeoff metrics?

Next steps:
- Monday 2027-06-21 10:00 PT: 30-minute sync (we will send the calendar invite and agenda now).
- By EOB Monday: Redwood will circulate the bakeoff test plan, measurement rubric, and a draft of the amendment (proposed_terms_STRATUS_v3.docx).

Samir — we want to make the procurement conversation defensible for your team. If you want, I can have Ben run a quick cost/term sensitivity table to show trade-offs between committed volumes and unit pricing ahead of the meeting.

Jordan Blake
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: proposed_terms_STRATUS_v3.docx]
